primitives.name: SVG Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: | ADOPT NOW | LIVE | | 2 | **SVGO** (npm/CLI) | Drop into build pipeline to strip/optimize every SVG (logos, icons, illustrations) → cuts Vercel bandwidth + improves LCP.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'$S$': 'SVG shape or path', '$\\text{Area}(S)$': 'Dimensionless area of the SVG shape'}
primitives.assumptions: Assumes the SVG contains redundant path data; clipping paths are well-formed; the optimization preserves visual fidelity within perceptual thresholds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At high-cardinality icon sets, the optimization may fail if the SVG contains raster elements embedded in XML.

layer2.mapping: Maps to lossy compression in information theory, where the goal is to minimize description length while maintaining a bounded distortion threshold.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage reduction in SVG file size and its impact on Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)

primitives.name: Image Compression
primitives.verbatim_quote: | ADOPT NOW | LIVE | | 3 | **Squoosh** | Compress/convert hero + OG + content images to WebP/AVIF before commit → Core Web Vitals (LCP) + bandwidth for the SEO content play.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'$I$': 'Original image', '$\\mathcal{F}_{\\text{JPEG}}(I)$': 'JPEG compression function', "$C(I')$": 'Compressed image size after optimization'}
primitives.assumptions: Assumes the image is in RGB color space; the compression ratio is controlled by a quality factor; perceptual metrics like MS-SSIM are used to ensure visual similarity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Compression fails when the input image contains fine textures or sharp edges, leading to blocking artifacts that degrade perceived quality.

layer2.mapping: Maps to rate-distortion theory in communications, where the objective is to find the minimum bitrate $R(D)$ that achieves a target distortion $D$.
layer2.telemetry: Compression ratio (original size / compressed size) and its effect on page load time

primitives.name: API Debugging
primitives.verbatim_quote: | ADOPT NOW | LIVE | | 5 | **Webhook.site** | Inspect raw Stripe webhook payloads + The Odds API callbacks during local dev before wiring server handlers.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes the payload is well-formed JSON or form-data; the debugging endpoint is stateless; the observed data is a sample path of API request-response cycles.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Debugging fails when the payload is encrypted or obfuscated; the primitive requires manual inspection for complex nested structures.

layer2.mapping: Maps to event sequence analysis in stochastic processes, where the state space consists of HTTP status codes and response headers.
layer2.telemetry: Latency between request and response (in milliseconds) and error rate of parsed payloads

primitives.name: UI Component Library
primitives.verbatim_quote: | ADOPT NOW | LIVE | | 6 | **shadcn/ui** | Copy-paste React + Tailwind + Radix components (own the code, no dep lock-in) → build the picks UI, paywall gates, dashboards fast and accessibly.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes the components follow atomic design principles; accessibility features are baked into the base implementation; the library has zero external dependencies.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Component reuse breaks down when the application requires highly customized, domain-specific visualizations that are not covered by the library.

layer2.mapping: Maps to reusable subroutines in numerical analysis, where the goal is to minimize development time by leveraging pre-verified code blocks.
layer2.telemetry: Number of lines of code saved per UI feature and pass/fail score on automated accessibility tests
